title: Toward construction-specialized, small language models: The interplay of domain adaptation, model scale and data volume
task: 施工领域语言模型适配策略与规模比较
inputData: 施工规范的抽取式问答 + 安全指南的开放式问答数据
contribution: 系统比较Prompt、RAG、任务微调以及预训练+微调四类领域适配策略在大、中、小不同规模语言模型和不同数据量条件下的效果，给出施工专用小模型的规模—数据—适配策略选择依据。
abstract: The study develops construction-specialized language models at multiple scales and evaluates four domain-adaptation strategies—prompt engineering, RAG, task-specific fine-tuning, and pretraining plus fine-tuning—under zero-shot through many-shot data regimes. It shows that sufficiently adapted small models can outperform larger models while being substantially faster.
methodology: Four representative adaptation strategies are implemented across large-, medium- and small-scale language models: prompt engineering and RAG as training-free approaches, and task-specific fine-tuning plus domain pretraining-and-fine-tuning as training-required approaches. Evaluation uses a construction QA benchmark containing 855 extractive QA pairs derived from construction specifications and 694 open-ended QA pairs based on safety guidelines. Performance is studied across zero-shot, few-shot, medium-shot and many-shot supervision regimes to isolate interactions between model capacity, adaptation strategy and available data.
results: A small-scale model using pretraining plus fine-tuning achieves the strongest overall specialized performance, improving F1 by 14.6% and S-BERT similarity by 10.2% while providing roughly fourfold faster inference than larger-scale counterparts. Large models with prompt/RAG are strongest when labeled data are scarce, whereas training-based adaptation increasingly favors smaller models as supervision becomes sufficient.
taskEn: Comparison of construction-domain LM adaptation strategies, model scale, and data volume
inputDataEn: Extractive QA from construction specifications plus open-ended QA from construction safety guidelines
operationEvidence: RAG is an explicitly implemented and evaluated adaptation arm that retrieves construction-domain evidence for QA; ordinary QA prose is not separately coded as generation.
